messages.content: You are a precise writing assistant for professional cover letters. Follow the instructions exactly and return only what is asked.

You write the BODY paragraphs of a professional cover letter. The greeting,
header, date, and sign-off are added separately - do not write them.
Use only the candidate's experience and skills that are RELEVANT to this
specific role; do not add unrelated skills or filler.

Write 2-3 short paragraphs, separated by a blank line:
1. Why the candidate is a strong fit for THIS role at THIS company.
2. One or two concrete skills/experiences that match the job description.
3. A brief, confident closing that thanks them and invites a conversation.

Candidate profile:
Name: Aaliyah Huang
Location: San Francisco, CA
Education:
  - B.S. Computer Science, UC Berkeley, 2021
Experience:
  - Frontend Engineer, Nimbus: Built and maintained a component library used by 12 product teams; improved Lighthouse performance scores by 35% and led accessibility remediation to WCAG 2.1 AA.
Projects:
  - Portfolio [Next.js, GraphQL]
Skills: React, TypeScript, Node.js, GraphQL, accessibility, design systems

Job details:
Company: Bright Labs
Role: Frontend Engineer
Description:
Bright Labs builds analytics tools used by thousands of teams, and we're hiring a Frontend Engineer to help make them fast and accessible. You'll build responsive, accessible interfaces in React and TypeScript, own and evolve our design system, and partner closely with product and design to ship features end to end. You'll also integrate our GraphQL APIs and help set the bar for performance across the product. We're looking for 3+ years of frontend experience, strong React and TypeScript, experience maintaining a design system, and familiarity with WCAG accessibility standards and performance optimization. GraphQL and Next.js are a plus.

These profile terms match this job - center the letter on them: React, TypeScript, GraphQL, accessibility, design systems, performance, product, frontend, js, next, wcag, engineer.

Return only the body paragraphs - no greeting, no sign-off.

I was genuinely excited to see the Frontend Engineer opening at Bright Labs. Building accessible, high-performance React interfaces is exactly the work I care most about, and the idea of doing it on analytics tools that thousands of teams rely on is a strong pull for me.

Much of what you describe mirrors my day-to-day. At Nimbus I built and maintained the component library that twelve product teams depended on, so owning and evolving a design system end to end is familiar territory. I work in TypeScript by default and partner closely with product and design to take features from idea to ship.

Your emphasis on accessibility and performance is where I do some of my best work. I led our WCAG 2.1 AA remediation so the whole product met the standard, and I raised our Lighthouse performance scores by 35% through focused profiling and code-splitting. I'm also comfortable wiring up GraphQL APIs, which lines up with your stack.

I'd welcome the chance to bring that same focus on quality and inclusive design to Bright Labs. Thank you for considering my application, and I'd love to talk more about how I can help your team.
